decoder: reproduction.obs_loop.decode_parent_pcm -> librosa.load(sr=16000, mono=True) then int16; ffmpeg is absent by design and was not used

derived_from.built_from: the SEALED v1 test WAV bytes, each re-hashed against the committed D1 media supplement before it was read; no parent MP3 was opened and no decoder ran
derived_from.id_rule: <call>-<segment>@ts2; the published segment key is recovered by splitting on '@', so the reference layer and the paired join against the sealed test arm are both exact and no id collides with the v1 population's
derived_from.rule: exactly 2.0 s (32,000 zero samples) appended to the sealed test v1 clip; nothing is removed and nothing is re-decoded

rule_implementation.note: the dev1500 builder's own transform, imported and pinned by content, so this population's bytes are produced by the same rule and the same code as the dev1500 tail-silence-2s variant

split_role_basis: The SAME 2,735 published ESB test utterances the sealed 2026-09-05 SAEA-E22-ESB-SHORTFORM-ALIGNMENT-V1 flight already read, re-encoded by one deterministic rule from the sealed v1 bytes. The 2026-09-04 owner decision re-designated these six calls calibration-exposed after that one read, and contracts.plan.STAGE2_SPLIT_ROLES admits only 'discovery' and 'dev', so 'dev' -- the role that means usable for calibration and never for final reporting -- is how calibration-exposed reaches the machine, exactly as the sealed test roster already expresses it. Building this media is NOT the second read: the flight that sends it needs the owner's explicit GO and its own exposure row. The 109 remaining confirmatory calls are not named, loaded, decoded or read.
